life_summary: Howard William Hunter was born November 14, 1907, in Boise, Idaho, to a business and professional family. He was educated at Brigham Young University and received training in business and accounting, becoming a certified public accountant. Hunter enjoyed music and played the violin, maintaining artistic pursuits throughout his life. He established himself as a respected accountant and businessman in California, where he spent much of his career before his ecclesiastical service became his primary focus. Hunter served in business and professional capacities in Los Angeles and maintained a reputation for integrity and careful financial management. He balanced commercial success with significant church service, demonstrating that secular achievement and religious commitment could coexist.
church_summary: Hunter served a mission location not specifically documented in available sources. Ordained an apostle in 1959, he became known for his diplomatic approach, reconciliation efforts, and emphasis on Christ-like living and temple attendance. He served as president of the Los Angeles Temple and later as president of the Oakland Temple. As church president from June 1994 until his death in March 1995, Hunter served the shortest presidency in church history at nine months. During his brief tenure, he prioritized temple attendance and Christ-centered discipleship. He dedicated the Bountiful Utah Temple, the Orlando Florida Temple, and presided at the dedication of the BYU Jerusalem Center. His emphasis on reconciliation and invitation to return to church became defining themes.
